hypothesis: dW-only whole-step neutrality is caused by HOST dispatch overhead of the Python aten::mm override, not by lack of kernel gain
experiment: single-factor control in the real BGE-M3 entry: native vs dw_only_routed (Triton dW kernel via Python route) vs dw_native_contig (NATIVE mm on an explicit contiguous() copy, SAME Python route + SAME mm.out fallback + SAME output allocation); profiler OFF; 3 real steps (27,052/31,454/35,506 tokens); two independent reps with rotated group order

int_hits_recorded.NOTE: hit counts are NOT reliably attributable: IMPL libraries stack, the later-registered one captures the earlier group's count (1056/2112 swap between reps). Timing is unaffected (each group timed in its own pass).

findings: HOST DISPATCH: registering the Python IMPL override doubles host aten::mm events (5,776 -> 11,120) and host CPU time (308.5 -> 611.1 ms per step, +303 ms). This is ~10x larger than the ~25-33 ms/step kernel-level saving, so the Python routing layer consumes any dW kernel gain.
PYTHON ROUTING DECISION ITSELF is cheap (microbench ~0.65 us/call x 5,768 = ~3.8 ms/step) - the cost is the aten->Python->aten double traversal, not the shape lookup.
OUTPUT ALLOCATION (torch.empty + mm.out vs mm) is NOT the cause: microbench delta within +-10 us on the dW shapes.

native+contiguous() is NOT faster than native (6 paired diffs: 4 positive, rep1 consistently ~+57 ms): the explicit copy costs more than the transposed-view penalty it removes. So the FlagGems 'gain' is not a free layout effect either.

KERNEL GAIN RECONCILIATION: FG mm internally calls .contiguous() on non-contiguous inputs. On a CONTIGUOUS operand FG == native (102.6 vs 98.6 TF/s); on the real TRANSPOSED VIEW native drops to 82.7 TF/s while FG stays 102.4. The apparent gain is therefore 'native mm is slow on transposed views', which native+copy does not recover because the copy itself costs.
Microbenchmarks on this device are UNSTABLE across runs (same shape measured 0.42 ms and 1.69 ms in different processes) - whole-step paired runs are the only reliable comparison.

verdict.quantified: ~303 ms/step host overhead from the Python IMPL override (profiler-on diagnostic) vs <=33 ms/step available kernel saving
verdict.candidate_kernel_gain: small and shape-dependent; on real transposed-view operands FG is faster (102 vs 83 TF/s) but native+contiguous is not a substitute (copy cost)
verdict.whole_step_result: dw_only vs native all6: median 7.0 ms, range [-22.7, 33.4] (sign flips); native+contig vs native: median 33.8 ms (mostly slower)
verdict.training_impact: a library-level (non-Python) registration that avoids the aten->Python double traversal is the only way the dW gain could reach the whole step; NOT available in this environment (FlagGems mm is a Python function) - listed as the next falsifiable test, NOT executed

assistance_needed: a C++/library-level hook to call the dW kernel without per-call Python dispatch, or Triton-compile-free native support for transposed-view operands
